title: Making my sci-fi roguelite
author: i-am-groo0oot
selftext:
I’m making Station Null, a side-view action roguelite set on an abandoned research station. Kills charge up a blink attack that lets you cut through enemies.

I’m building it in Beeloop Engine. I started with a [game design document](https://postimg.cc/JGcN3pKD) to work out the mechanics, then put together a [moodboard](https://postimg.cc/GHJFPXzY) to keep the art consistent

I also worked out the [backstory](https://postimg.cc/QHkQgfS1), [character details](https://postimg.cc/hfbL82Mb) and [timeline](https://postimg.cc/mtNY3mV7). Probably spent more time on this part than I needed to.

From there, I built out the [asset library](https://postimg.cc/Mvb709tY). Characters started as [concept sheets,](https://postimg.cc/8jBRdZwt) then became [sprites](https://postimg.cc/rKC1GfgH).

  
For animations, I [picked movements](https://postimg.cc/mtNY3mVX) on a 3D mannequin and used those to make the [character’s animations](https://postimg.cc/RWScgwbp).  


Once the assets were ready, I put the [levels together](https://postimg.cc/v4YW05SX) in the editor.

Getting it looking good was fairly quick. Most of the work went into testing and tweaking the movement, enemy behaviour and animation timing until the fights felt good.



You can try the demo at [beeloop.ai](https://beeloop.ai). Would love to hear what you think.
